land.text: the Alt Urgell core: La Seu d'Urgell, the Valira valleys of Andorra, Organyà and Oliana (13 cells)

predecessors.note: The page: 'The county of Urgell was carved by the Franks out of a former section of the Mark of Toulouse'; the infobox says 'Start: 785' and 'Preceded by: Carolingian Empire', the text that the Alt Urgell area joined the Carolingian Empire 'between 785 and 790'; the first count, Borrell, is dated 798-820. 798 is used because the emirate-of-cordoba dossier has Urgell and Cerdanya pass to the Franks in 798 ('Urgell and Cerdanya were added in 798').

land.text: the county's land as the counts held it in 1413 (the 1236 keyframe, 17 cells): 'The county of Urgell was extinguished and absorbed by the Crown of Aragon in 1413'

successors.note: The Crown absorbs the county in 1413 (County page). The Crown of Aragon dossier holds the 18 cells from 1236 (Cliopatria's shape); this dossier has James I hold the county directly 1231-1235 and the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants hold the 17 cells (Andorra left in 1133) as the Crown's fief 1236-1412, so the Crown must subtract them for 1236-1412, record the vassal_start and gain them in 1413. The Cliopatria shapes of 1279-1808 (one cell, Andorra) are not this state: see co-principality-of-andorra.

capitals.name: La Seu d'Urgell
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: La Seu d'Urgell (first), later Balaguer' (the page dates neither). Coordinates are the researcher's.

capitals.name: Balaguer
capitals.note: Ermengol VI 'conquered Balaguer in 1105 and made it his capital' (Ermengol VI page); the Balaguer page says 1106 and that it 'remained so for subsequent counts of Urgell'. Coordinates are the researcher's. The Ermengol IV page dates the recapture of Balaguer to 1102 under Ermengol V.

rulers.name: Borrell
rulers.note: First count, as the infobox lists him; the page gives no counts for 820-870 (Wilfred's grandfather and father are not on the page opened).

rulers.name: Wilfred the Hairy
rulers.note: 'at an assembly at Attigny in June 870, Charles the Bald' made him count of Urgell and Cerdanya; he 'died in battle on 11 August 897'.

rulers.name: Sunifred II
rulers.note: Died without descendants; the county passed to his nephew Borrell II.

rulers.name: Borrell II
rulers.note: Count of Barcelona, Girona and Ausona from 945 and of Urgell from 948 (Borrell II page); the County page: 'Borrell II's testament separated Urgell from the House of Barcelona' in 992.

rulers.name: Ermengol III
rulers.note: 'was the Count of Urgell from 1038 to his death'; 'He died before 12 April 1065' (Ermengol III page).

rulers.name: Ermengol IV
rulers.note: The Ermengol IV page says 'count of Urgell from 1066 to his death' and 'It was not until 1075 that Ermengol had genuine control'.

rulers.name: Ermengol VI
rulers.note: 'was the count of Urgell from 1102 until his death' on 20 June 1154.

rulers.name: Aurembiaix
rulers.note: The Aurembiaix page: 'Countess of Urgell from 1208'; 'In 1209, Aurembiaix became countess under the regency of her mother'; displaced by Guerau IV of Cabrera after 1213; back in 1228-1229; died 1231 'without descendants at Balaguer'. 'Urgell went to Peter' (of Portugal), who exchanged it with James I (James I page).

rulers.name: Ponç I (Ponç IV of Cabrera)
rulers.note: 'In 1236, Jaume I recognized Ponç IV of Cabrera as successor'. The county is a dependent title in the Crown of Aragon from here.

rulers.name: Ermengol X
rulers.note: The page names no count for 1314-1336.

rulers.name: Jaume II
rulers.note: The last count; his revolt against Ferdinand I of Aragon ended the county in 1413.

correction.text: the Alt Urgell core: La Seu d'Urgell, the Valira valleys of Andorra, Organyà and Oliana (13 cells)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 798-869: Cliopatria starts in 870 (Wilfred) although the page dates the first count (Borrell) to 798 and says the county 'would include 129 villages' in 839, with 'the Valira valleys (including Andorra and Sant Joan Fumat), the Segre riverine area, and valleys between El Pont de Bar and Oliana'. Cliopatria's 898 outline (13 cells: Seu d'Urgell, Andorra, Organyà, Oliana) fits that description and stands in; the Cerdanya cells join in 870. The infobox gives no area.

870-877, 5,354 km2 (22 cells): Urgell with Cerdanya, the two counties Charles the Bald gave Wilfred 'at an assembly at Attigny in June 870'. The 898 outline is the nine cells smaller after Cerdanya went to Miró in 897. No infobox area on any page.

correction.text: Urgell and Cerdanya only (the 870 outline) for 878-895; Barcelona, Girona, Besalú and Ausona are the other counties' land

keyframe_review.note: 878-895, 15,405 km2 (62 cells, the largest Urgell shape): the shape holds the whole patrimony of Wilfred the Hairy ('received the counties of Barcelona, Girona, and Besalú in 878'; Ausona from 886), not the county of Urgell. Barcelona, Girona, Besalú and Ausona are drawn by county-of-barcelona and county-of-besalu, which would be double-covered; the 870 outline (Urgell and Cerdanya) is used for Urgell. Hence the 15,405 km2 is 3 times the 5,354 km2 of the county proper.

correction.text: Urgell and Cerdanya only (the 870 outline) for 896-897

keyframe_review.note: 896-897, 15,286 km2 (63 cells): the same Wilfred patrimony (the Alt Empordà cells now belong to Cliopatria's Rosellón row). The 870 outline is used. Wilfred 'died in battle on 11 August 897'; Miró took Cerdanya and Conflent, Sunifred Urgell, and the 898 outline is Urgell alone.

898-959, 3,260 km2 (13 cells): right for 898-947, Urgell under Sunifred II (897-948). 'In 948, Borrell inherited Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II' and held it with Barcelona, Girona and Ausona until the separation of 992: the shape does not hold 948-959 as a state of its own because the Barcelona dossier draws these cells in its 948-959 keyframe.

correction.text: the Urgell core inside the County of Barcelona's shape, 948-991

keyframe_review.note: 961-969, 3,260 km2: the same 13 cells. Urgell was held by the counts of Barcelona from 948 to 992 ('In 948, Borrell inherited Urgell'; the County page: Borrell II's testament separated Urgell from the House of Barcelona in 992); Cliopatria draws the cells twice, in Urgell 961-969 and in Barcelona's 960, 970 and 990 shapes. They belong to Barcelona's drawing for 948-991 (and Cliopatria has no Urgell shape for 970-999).

New keyframe for 992-999: 'Borrell II's testament separated Urgell from the House of Barcelona, giving it to Ermengol I' (992); Cliopatria resumes Urgell only in 1000. The 1000 outline is applied back to 992. The Borrell II page dates the division of Borrell's territory to 'From 988'.
1000-1014, 3,260 km2, the 13-cell core under Ermengol I (992-1010) and Ermengol II (1010-1038). No infobox area.
1015-1027, 3,238 km2: the same 13 cells (only the vertices differ); no page explains a change in 1015.

New keyframe for 1028-1039: Cliopatria has no Urgell shape (its County of Ribagorza row, 85,501 and 171,828 km2, covers the Pyrenees in those years) but Ermengol II reigned 1010-1038 and Ermengol III from 1038, with no page giving a change of extent. The 1015 outline is applied.

correction.text: the 1040 shape unchanged, holding from 1050; the 1015 outline for 1040-1049

keyframe_review.note: 1040-1065, 4,002 km2 (15 cells): adds two cells (0.94 E 41.90 N and 0.74 E 41.88 N, the Camarasa-Cubells side of the Segre). The Ermengol III page dates the gain to 1050: 'occupying, in 1050, Camarasa and Cubells after taking them from Yusuf of Lleida'. So the shape holds 1050 onwards and the 1015 outline 1040-1049.
1066-1071, 3,954 km2: the same 15 cells; the Ermengol IV page dates his reign from 1066 ('count of Urgell from 1066 to his death').

correction.text: the 1072 shape unchanged, holding from 1076; the 1066 outline for 1072-1075

keyframe_review.note: 1072-1093, 4,384 km2 (17 cells): adds two cells (Agramunt, and the lower Sió basin towards Balaguer). The page dates it later: 'In 1076, having brought the nobles to submission, he began a Reconquista of his own', 'taking the basin of the river Sió with the villages of Agramunt and Almenar that year'. So the shape holds from 1076 and the 1066 outline for 1072-1075. (The Taifa of Lérida page has Peter of Aragon take Almenar between 1087 and 1093 and Ermengol IV attack Balaguer in 1089, 'possibly even taking the city temporarily'.)
1094-1098, 4,289 km2: the same 17 cells. The Ermengol IV page has 'Linyola and Belcaire in 1091' (inside the lower Sió cell Cliopatria already holds); no cell changes.
1099-1110, 4,384 km2: the same 17 cells; Ermengol V reigned 1092-1102 (County page list) and the page opened for his son gives Balaguer in 1105.

1111-1125, 4,599 km2 (18 cells): adds one cell (0.67 E 41.73 N, west of Balaguer). Ermengol VI 'conquered Balaguer in 1105' (the Balaguer page: 1106); the Cliopatria cell nearest Balaguer is already in the shape from 1072, and no page dates the added cell, so the shape stands. Thin item tried 2026-10-31: the Balaguer page names no village or castle added around 1111 and the Ermengol IV page names none near Balaguer; the cell stays undated (verdict ok, a gap).

1126-1151, 4,504 km2 (18 cells): right for 1126-1132. 'In 1133, Ermengol ceded Andorra to the Bishop of Urgell' (Ermengol VI page, re-read 2026-10-31; the Andorra page has 988, the County page 'the twelfth century'), so from 1133 the Andorra cell leaves the shape (ledger 1133 loss; keyframe county-of-urgell_1133). 'In 1149, he assisted Raymond Berenguer in the conquest and repopulation of Lleida, receiving one-third of the city': a third share inside the Lleida cell that county-of-barcelona gains from the Almoravids in 1149; it is not drawn as a second owner (the 1149 ledger event was lowered to this note on 2026-10-31).

correction.text: the 1126 shape unchanged, holding 1126-1132 only (18 cells, Andorra still the count's); from 1133 see county-of-urgell_1133
the 1126 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133

keyframe_review.note: 1133-1151, 17 cells (about 4,300 km2): 'In 1133, Ermengol ceded Andorra to the Bishop of Urgell.' (Ermengol VI page). The removed cell is the one Cliopatria draws alone for the Andorran valleys from 1279 (see co-principality-of-andorra). The 1149 third of Lleida is not a separate owner (see keyframe 1126).

1152-1168, 4,552 km2: the same 18 cells. Ermengol VI died 20 June 1154, Ermengol VII reigned 1154-1184 (County page list). Adjusted 2026-10-31: less the Andorra cell, ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133 (Ermengol VI page), so 17 cells. The 1149 third of Lleida (Ermengol VI page) is a share inside Barcelona's cell and is not drawn as a second owner.

keyframe_review.note: 1169-1176, 4,623 km2: the same 18 cells; no page dates a change. Adjusted 2026-10-31: less the Andorra cell, ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133 (Ermengol VI page), so 17 cells.

keyframe_review.note: 1177-1187, 4,528 km2: the same 18 cells. Adjusted 2026-10-31: less the Andorra cell, ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133 (Ermengol VI page), so 17 cells.

keyframe_review.note: 1192-1201, 4,718 km2: the same 18 cells. Ermengol VIII reigned 1184-1209. Adjusted 2026-10-31: less the Andorra cell, ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133 (Ermengol VI page), so 17 cells.

correction.text: the 1192 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133

the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133, holding 1202-1230; 1231-1235 the Crown's direct hold (no Urgell shape); from 1236 see county-of-urgell_1236

keyframe_review.note: 1202-1235, 4,836 km2: right to 1230 apart from the Andorra cell (17 cells from 1133). The Aurembiaix page: she died 'without descendants at Balaguer' in 1231 and 'Urgell went to Peter'; the James I page: 'On her death in 1231, James exchanged the Balearic Islands for Urgell with her widower, Peter of Portugal.' 1231-1235 the land is James I's own; from 1236 the counts of Cabrera hold it again as the Crown's fief (keyframe county-of-urgell_1236). The page's 'maximum extent' list (Alt Urgell, Noguera, Solsonès, Pla d'Urgell, Baix Urgell, Andorra) is wider than the 18 cells, which lack Solsona and the Pla d'Urgell.

correction.text: the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133: the land of the county as the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants held it from 1236 to 1413

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1236-1412: Cliopatria has no County of Urgell shape for 1236-1278 and ends the row in 1235 (its Crown of Aragon shape holds the 18 cells from 1236). The County page (re-read 2026-10-31): 'After a period of dynastic squabbles Jaume I acknowledged Ponç IV of Cabrera as the successor to the County of Urgell'; counts listed Ponç I 1236-1243 to Jaume II 1408-1413; 'The county of Urgell was extinguished and absorbed by the Crown of Aragon in 1413'. The page names no fief; the James I page has Aurembiaix 'agreed to hold Urgell in fief for him' (1229), so the 17 cells are drawn as the counts' fief of the Crown (vassal tint), confidence 2. No page gives an area; about 4,300 km2 by cell count.

region.text: the Alt Urgell core: La Seu d'Urgell, the Valira valleys of Andorra, Organyà and Oliana (13 cells)

ledger.note: 798: the county of Urgell begins under its first count, Borrell. The infobox gives 'Start: 785' and 'Borrell, 798-820 (first count)'; the text puts the Alt Urgell area in the Carolingian Empire 'between 785 and 790' and says the Franks 'carved' the county 'out of a former section of the Mark of Toulouse'. The year 798 is the first count's; the extent is Cliopatria's 898 outline as a stand-in.

region.text: Cerdanya: the nine cells of the 870 outline that the 898 outline lacks

ledger.note: June 870: Charles the Bald gives Wilfred the Hairy Urgell and Cerdanya. 'at an assembly at Attigny in June 870, Charles the Bald made their cousins, Wilfred the Hairy' counts of Urgell and Cerdanya (the tool's paraphrase). Cerdanya joins Urgell; the page gives the counties, not an outline.

region.text: Cerdanya: the nine cells of the 870 outline that the 898 outline lacks

ledger.note: 11 August 897: Wilfred dies and Miró takes Cerdanya. 'Wilfred died in battle on 11 August 897'; Miró 'over Cerdanya and Conflent; and Sunifred over Urgell'; Wilfred Borrell and Sunyer ruled Barcelona, Girona and Ausona. Cerdanya-Berga is county-of-berga's land from 897.

region.text: the Alt Urgell core: La Seu d'Urgell, the Valira valleys of Andorra, Organyà and Oliana (13 cells)

ledger.note: 948: Borrell II of Barcelona inherits Urgell. 'In 948, Borrell inherited Urgell from his uncle Sunifred II' (no month). The County page: 'Sunifred II died, and the county went to Borrell II, Count of Barcelona, Girona and Osona'. Urgell is held in union with Barcelona until 992; the Barcelona dossier draws the cells.

region.text: the Alt Urgell core: La Seu d'Urgell, the Valira valleys of Andorra, Organyà and Oliana (13 cells)

ledger.note: 992: Urgell separates from Barcelona under Ermengol I. 'Borrell II's testament separated Urgell from the House of Barcelona, giving it to Ermengol I' (the page lists Ermengol I 992-1010). The Borrell II page says only 'From 988, Borrell's sons Ramon Borrell and Ermengol appear as rulers in a divided territory, with Ermengol as count of Urgell'.

region.text: Camarasa and Cubells, the two cells Cliopatria adds in 1040

ledger.note: 1050: Ermengol III takes Camarasa and Cubells. 'occupying, in 1050, Camarasa and Cubells after taking them from Yusuf of Lleida'. The taifa-of-lerida dossier has no matching loss.

union.text: the lower Sió basin towards Balaguer

region.text: the basin of the river Sió with Agramunt and Almenar: the two cells Cliopatria adds in 1072

ledger.note: 1076: Ermengol IV begins a Reconquista of his own. 'In 1076, having brought the nobles to submission, he began a Reconquista of his own', 'taking the basin of the river Sió with the villages of Agramunt and Almenar that year'. The Taifa of Lérida page has Peter of Aragon take Almenar between 1087 and 1093: the pages disagree on Almenar.

region.text: Linyola and Belcaire (Bellcaire d'Urgell), south of the Sió

ledger.note: 1091: Ermengol IV takes Linyola and Belcaire. The page: 'Linyola and Belcaire in 1091'. It does not name the owner; the Taifa of Lérida (to 1102) held the Segre plain, so it is the counterpart (the researcher's reading). Inside a cell Cliopatria already holds.

1105: Ermengol VI conquers Balaguer and makes it his capital. 'conquered Balaguer in 1105 and made it his capital' (the Balaguer page: 'conquered from the Moors by Ermengol VI of Urgell in 1106'). The pages do not name the owner; the Taifa of Lérida page has Lérida fall to the Almoravids in 1102 or 1110, so the Almoravids are the counterpart at confidence 2. Re-read 2026-10-31: the Ermengol IV page dates the recapture of Balaguer to 1102 under Ermengol V ('the recapture of Balaguer, which occurred during the reign of his son, Ermengol V, in 1102'); the Pedro Ansúrez page (exile in Urgell 1103-1108) says 'He took an active part in the conquest of Balaguer' without a year or an owner; the Balaguer page does not say who held the town. The owner stays the Almoravids at confidence 2.
1105: the seat moves from La Seu d'Urgell to Balaguer. 'made it his capital'; 'it remained so for subsequent counts of Urgell' (Balaguer page).

region.text: Andorra: the valleys of Andorra, Cliopatria's one-cell shape of 1279-1808

ledger.note: 1133: Ermengol VI cedes Andorra to the Bishop of Urgell. 'In 1133, Ermengol ceded Andorra to the Bishop of Urgell.' (Ermengol VI page). The County page has only 'in the twelfth century' and the Andorra page 'In 988, Count Borrell II of Urgell gave the Andorran valleys to the Diocese of Urgell in exchange for land in Cerdanya'; 1133 is used because it names the count and the year. The counterpart is the bishop's lordship, written 'Bishop of Urgell' as county-of-foix and co-principality-of-andorra write it (suggested slug bishopric-of-urgell, no dossier yet); it holds the valleys until the paréage of 1278 (co-principality-of-andorra).

region.text: the county less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133, 17 cells

ledger.note: 1231: the county passes to James I of Aragon. 'On her death in 1231, James exchanged the Balearic Islands for Urgell with her widower, Peter of Portugal.' (James I page, re-read 2026-10-31). Aurembiaix had held Urgell from James since 1229: 'She surrendered Lleida to James and agreed to hold Urgell in fief for him.' She died at Balaguer in 1231 and 'Urgell went to Peter' (Aurembiaix page). James holds the county directly until 1236, when the counts of Cabrera take it back as his fief (next events).

1236: James I recognises Ponç IV of Cabrera as count. 'In 1236, Jaume I recognized Ponç IV of Cabrera as successor' after the first dynasty ended with Aurembiaix in 1231; the House of Cabrera, then Cardona and the Aragonese infants, hold the county as a dependent title to 1413.

region.text: the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133: the land of the county as the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants held it from 1236 to 1413

ledger.note: 1236: the county returns to the counts of Urgell under the Crown. 'After a period of dynastic squabbles Jaume I acknowledged Ponç IV of Cabrera as the successor to the County of Urgell.' (County of Urgell page, re-read 2026-10-31). The year and the successor are the page's; the land is my reading (the 1202 shape less Andorra). Cliopatria's Crown of Aragon shape adds the 18 cells in 1236, which crown-of-aragon repairs by subtracting them for 1236-1412 (see notes).

region.text: the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133: the land of the county as the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants held it from 1236 to 1413

ledger.note: 1236: Ponç IV of Cabrera holds the county as the Crown's fief. The County page names no fief or vassalage; the James I page has Aurembiaix 'agree to hold Urgell in fief for him' in 1229 and the page has the county 'absorbed by the Crown of Aragon in 1413', so the counts are drawn as the Crown's vassal (lighter tint) from 1236 to 1413. Mirror: crown-of-aragon records a vassal_start with counterpart county-of-urgell.

region.text: the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133: the land of the county as the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants held it from 1236 to 1413

ledger.note: 1413: the counts' fief ends with the extinction of the county. 'The county of Urgell was extinguished and absorbed by the Crown of Aragon in 1413'; the last count, Jaume II, had revolted against Ferdinand I (the page's wording in the infobox). Pairs the 1236 vassal_start.

region.text: the 1202 shape less the Andorra valleys (17 cells), which Ermengol VI ceded to the Bishop of Urgell in 1133: the land of the county as the counts of Cabrera, Cardona and the Aragonese infants held it from 1236 to 1413

ledger.note: 1413: the Crown of Aragon absorbs the County of Urgell. 'The county of Urgell was extinguished and absorbed by the Crown of Aragon in 1413' (County of Urgell page, re-read 2026-10-31). Mirror: crown-of-aragon gains the cells in 1413.

region.text: the county's land as the counts held it in 1413 (the 1236 keyframe, 17 cells), absorbed by the Crown

ledger.note: 1413: the county is absorbed by the Crown of Aragon. Infobox 'End: 1413' and 'Succeeded by: Principality of Catalonia'; absorbed 'after James II revolted against Ferdinand I'.

wars.name: Barbastro War of 1064
wars.outcome: Ermengol III 'took part in the Barbastro War of 1064 under the banner of his brother-in-law Sancho Ramírez of Aragon'; the page gives no land for Urgell.
wars.note: Considered and left without a zone: no Urgell cell changes.

wars.name: Ermengol IV's Reconquista in the Sió basin

union.text: the lower Sió basin towards Balaguer

zones.text: the basin of the river Sió with Agramunt and Almenar: the two cells Cliopatria adds in 1072
Linyola and Belcaire (Bellcaire d'Urgell), south of the Sió

wars.outcome: Ermengol IV took the Sió basin with Agramunt and Almenar in 1076 and Linyola and Belcaire in 1091.
wars.note: The page also dates the first control of his nobles to 1075. The Taifa of Lérida page has an attack towards Balaguer in 1089 ('possibly even taking the city temporarily') and the Aragonese taking Almenar in 1087-1093.

wars.name: Conquest of Balaguer (1105)
wars.outcome: Ermengol VI conquered Balaguer in 1105 (the Balaguer page: 1106) and made it his capital.
wars.note: Neither page names the owner of Balaguer.

wars.name: Siege of Zaragoza (1118)
wars.outcome: 'Ermengol collaborated with Alfonso the Battler in the 1118 capture of Zaragoza'; no Urgell border moved.

wars.name: Conquest of Lleida (1149)

zones.text: one third of the city of Lleida

wars.outcome: Lleida fell in 1149; Ermengol VI received one third of the city.
wars.note: The Taifa of Lérida page says only 'captured by the Catalans in 1149' and does not name the leaders. The 1149 gain event was lowered to a note on 2026-10-31: the Lleida cell is county-of-barcelona's only; the third share is not drawn as a second owner.

wars.name: Conquest of Almería (1147)
wars.outcome: Ermengol VI was 'against Almería in 1147' (and a commander at Albacete in 1146); no Urgell border moved.

wars.name: Guerau IV of Cabrera's seizure of Urgell
wars.outcome: After Peter II of Aragon's death (1213) Guerau IV of Cabrera, Aurembiaix's cousin, 'invaded the county and took control'; in 1228 she returned, in 1229 she rendered Lleida to James I and took Urgell back as his fief.
wars.note: A succession quarrel inside the county, with no second state to blend; the James I page dates the seizure to 1208 and 1220: the pages disagree.

certainty.note: A Pyrenean county: the pages name valleys, towns and comarques, never a boundary line; the outlines are Cliopatria's stand-ins. 1231-1235 the land is the Crown's direct hold and no Urgell shape is drawn; 1236-1412 the 17 cells are drawn as the counts' fief of the Crown (vassal tint, confidence 2).
